answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering detects sybils post hoc by linking accounts whose action sequences share rare feature pairs, like a marble of timing quirks and tool preferences. A sonnet of normal use leaves idiosyncratic traces that near-duplicate accounts cannot hide without costly mimicry. Once grouped, all linked accounts forfeit earned reputation, and the attacker must rebuild each identity's history from scratch, paying full organic-use costs per account. An atlas of these clusters also flags future signups sharing the same traces.
